question: Oxygen has _______ electrons in its outermost _______ shell.
solution:
The correct answer is __**6, L.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen is an element with atomic number 8.**
 
• The outermost shell of an atom is called the** valence shell.**
 
• The number of** electrons in the valence shell determines the chemical properties of an element.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Oxygen has 8 electrons in total**, with the first two shells having** 2 and 6 electrons respectively.**
 
• **Oxygen is in group 16 in the periodic table**, also known as the **chalcogens**, and it shares this group with **sulphur, selenium and tellurium.**
 
• Oxygen is a highly reactive element and will readily form chemical bonds with other elements in order to fill its valence shell.
 
• The most common form of oxygen on Earth is the **diatomic molecule, O2, **which contains** two oxygen atoms bonded together.**
 
• Oxygen is essential for life as we know it and is used by most organisms in the process of respiration to generate energy.
